b: Definition: a persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity and impulsivity that is more frequent and severe than in children of the same age.
Six or more symptoms in either group, starting before 12 years , present in two or more settings (home, school), and clearly impairing function.
Often presents at school age with poor concentration, forgetfulness, disorganisation, fidgeting, talking excessively, interrupting, and unsafe behaviour.
Rule out hearing and vision problems, chronic illness, seizures (absence), anxiety, depression, poor sleep, lead poisoning and a stressful home before diagnosing.

Management: parent training and behaviour therapy, classroom support and a structured routine. Stimulants (methylphenidate) or atomoxetine where symptoms are moderate to severe, with monitoring of growth, appetite, sleep and blood pressure.
